title: Hook: A Window to the World
text: Imagine being 10 years old. Every morning, you see your friends put on their uniforms, swing their bags over their shoulders, and run off to school, laughing. But you cannot join them. You have to sit by the window all day, just watching. Why might this happen? Meet Chuskit, a bright girl from Skitpo Pul village in the beautiful mountains of Ladakh.

title: Socratic Thinking: Thinking Together
text: Chuskit uses a wheelchair to move around. In a city with flat roads, a wheelchair moves smoothly. But Chuskit lives in a mountainous village. Think about the landscape of Ladakh. What are the natural obstacles that would make it almost impossible for a wheelchair to reach a school far away?

content.title: Discovery: Chuskit's Journey Map
content.description: The uneven path, the river stream, and the stairs at the school make the journey impossible for a wheelchair.

title: Reveal: The Power of a Community
text: Chuskit’s dream seemed impossible until a boy named Abdul noticed her. Instead of feeling sorry for her, he took action! He spoke to the Headmaster and teachers. Together with the children, they leveled the uneven dirt road. They built a strong wooden bridge across the cold river stream. They built a ramp at the school. In just a few days, they changed the world to fit Chuskit, rather than asking Chuskit to fit the world. This is called 'Accessibility'.

content.definition: The design of places and things so that everyone, including people with disabilities, can use them easily.
A chair with wheels, used by people who cannot walk due to illness, injury, or disability.

content.title: Teacher's Note
content.text: Emphasize to the students that 'disability' is often created by the environment, not the person. If a building has a ramp, a wheelchair user is just as capable of entering as anyone else.

content.title: Watch Out!
content.text: Many people think Chuskit couldn't go to school because she was 'sick'. That's incorrect! She was perfectly healthy and intelligent; her legs just didn't work. The real problem was the lack of a proper road and a bridge.

content.question: Knowledge Check: What did Abdul and the other children do to help Chuskit reach school?
options: They carried her on their backs every day.
They bought her a magical flying chair.
They leveled the path and built a bridge over the stream.
They told her to study at home with books.

title: Reflection: Your Turn to Reflect
text: Explain in your own words: How did Abdul's small idea change Chuskit's entire life? How do you think Chuskit felt on her first day of school?

title: Connection: Connecting to Our World
text: Think about the places around you—hospitals, malls, train stations, and your own school. Have you noticed ramps next to stairs? Have you seen special parking spots or large elevators? These are all ways we make our world accessible for everyone. When society builds the right path, everyone can travel forward.

content.title: Mastery: The Accessibility Challenge
content.description: Take a walk around your own school or neighborhood. Pretend you are on a wheelchair. Are there stairs without ramps? Are the doors wide enough? Draw a 'Dream School Map' that shows how you would make your school 100% accessible for a student like Chuskit.
